A1.justification: Despite the changed title and broader framing, both PDFs describe successive versions of the same research. All 20 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including appendices, equations and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 9 and Appendices A.7–A.10 report original synthetic experiments and MovieLens/Yahoo evaluations, including regret, clustering and sensitivity results.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix S report original synthetic and real-data evaluations. Appendix C.2 additionally documents a simulated two-agent estimation illustration.

M1.justification: BASS retains LBC's neighborhood pooling, OFUL arm selection and local ellipsoid tests. v3 introduces a gamma-relaxed threshold, a uniform-exploration mixture for analysis, and all-agent rounds in Algorithm 1; experiments still use asynchronous pulling. Its contradictory separation-indicator convention leaves the intended edge-removal rule unclear.

E1.justification: MovieLens, Yahoo and both synthetic environment families remain. The structured scenarios change from angles pi/3, pi/2 and 2pi/3 to pi/16 and 7pi/16, removing negative correlation coverage. v3 also adds an intermediate Gaussian noise level and a small two-agent estimation illustration.

E2.justification: The main comparator set remains DynUCB, CLUB, SCLUB, CMLB, Ind and, on synthetic data, Oracle. Uniform and both GreedyLBC variants disappear with the removal of v2 Appendix A.7's arm-selection comparison. Newly cited methods are not added to the empirical benchmarks.

E3.justification: Clustering evaluation changes from Adjusted Rand Index to graph F1. Real-data feature dimensionality changes from 20 to 10, the stated alpha search range narrows from [0.05, 5.0] to [0.1, 3.0], and the Gaussian benchmark changes from six clusters to three. These materially alter evaluation conditions.

E4.justification: v2's direct test of whether UCB separates clusters as effectively as Uniform and GreedyLBC is removed. v3 adds the two-agent estimation illustration and extends Gaussian noise sensitivity with sigma=1.0. Alpha sensitivity and the broader noise-robustness analyses remain, with revised settings.

E5.justification: Reported repetitions change from 20 to 50 for the principal synthetic and real-data experiments. v3 adds plus/minus entries and shaded bands to result reporting, but does not clearly identify their statistical meaning; v2 explicitly identifies its real-data error bars as standard deviations.

E6.justification: The benchmark results are extensively replaced under revised conditions. v2 reports perfect ARI on its structured three-cluster cases; v3 Table 3 reports BASS F1 values of 0.7–0.9. Table 2 reports BASS with delta=0.1 regret of 1096.8 and 1617.5. Real-data and Gaussian results also change. These are not comparable-setting gains or losses because metrics and configurations differ.

T1.justification: v3 substantially expands and revises the theory: it adds collaboration-error and instantaneous-regret bounds, pairwise separation-time bounds, and individual/network collaboration-phase regret analyses. Its clustered guarantee accommodates unequal cluster sizes and replaces v2's balanced-cluster analysis. Sections 5–6 and Appendices C–P contain new definitions and derivations, rather than merely reorganized proofs.

C1.justification: v2 centers its contribution on recovering clusters of identical agent parameters using exact ellipsoid separation. v3 instead claims adaptive, beneficial sample sharing without assumptions on parameter structure, founded on a bias–uncertainty trade-off. Cluster recovery becomes a special case, and novelty is repositioned around analyzing biased collaboration.

C2.justification: v3 develops temporary collaboration between unequal parameters as potentially beneficial, whereas v2 primarily analyzes incorrect clustering as a regret cost. It interprets separate collaboration-gain and bias terms, explains anisotropic similarity, and explicitly qualifies the separation analysis through forced exploration. Appendix O also acknowledges that its clustered bound is loose and does not capture adaptivity.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an authors' code-repository link, identifies Python, and reports 50 CPUs for one week instead of 20 CPUs for about 18 hours. It adds simulation details but omits v2's explicit 50% perturbation rule for constructing structured synthetic arms and its displayed separation-test derivatives. The missing construction detail does not establish an actual preprocessing change.

R1.justification: v3 adds recent work including Wang et al. (2023), Do et al. (2023), Cheng et al. (2023) and Yang et al. (2024). More substantially, it positions the contribution against Euclidean similarity and structural assumptions, with an explicit comparison of clustering assumptions in Appendix P.3, replacing the predominantly cluster-recovery positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Contributions move into Related Work, a two-agent preliminary explanation is introduced, and theory is reorganized around adaptive sharing. The single supplementary section becomes separately organized appendices with a contents page and notation summary.

P2.justification: v3 adds two ellipsoid illustrations, an algorithm flowchart, a theoretical comparison table and a notation table. Numerical tables replace the main clustering curves and real-data bar chart, while regret plots are redrawn and appendix panels are consolidated. Legends, uncertainty displays and figure arrangements also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful bias–uncertainty exposition, explicit result tables, more repetitions and code access information. However, unlike v2's consistent edge-removal sign, v3 Definition 5.1 and Appendix I identify Psi=1 as separation while Algorithm 1 removes Psi=0 edges, leaving the documented procedure inconsistent. The arm-selection ablation is also lost and new uncertainty displays are undefined. These substantive gains and harms prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
